name: Sensorik Ammertal GmbH
summary: Sensorik Ammertal is a privately held German sensor maker (150 staff, about 35 M EUR turnover) and our single source for pressure sensor part:350050. A financial investor bought it in June 2026, and price policy now comes from head office: reductions are frozen until December 2027, and moves above 2 % go to a pricing committee. It is financially sound and not dependent on us (we are 1.2 % of its turnover), but it is open on payment terms and call-off flexibility.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager or sales director up to 2 %. Above 2 %, the pricing committee (meets every two weeks). Head office under the new investor sets policy and has frozen price reductions until Dec 2027.

negotiation_pattern: At renewals it asks moderately and settles well below its ask: on average it asked +2.87 % and settled +0.43 %. Last round it asked +4.9 % and settled +3.1 %. The year before it asked +1.6 % and ended at -1.8 %. Before that it asked +2.1 % and ended at 0.0 %. So it gives ground in negotiation, but now hides behind head-office policy on price. Its 2026-09-02 quote held the price flat at 23.13 with the remark that no discounts are possible. In the latest meeting it refused price movement but offered flexibility on payment and call-offs.
wants: Keep list price intact (no visible reduction, per head-office directive)
Reliable and punctual payment, possibly faster payment
Contract continuity and volume security under the new owner's terms review
Room to fit its own schedule via call-off rules (its OTD has slipped)
protects: unit_price (head-office freeze on reductions until Dec 2027; quote remark says no discounts)
Any move above 2 % without pricing-committee approval
Possibly new terms that the investor wants to tighten (its planned review of prices and terms)

trades.give: payment_days: commit to punctual payment at 30 days, or shorter terms with a skonto
trades.get: A skonto of about 2 % for early payment, giving an effective reduction without touching list price
trades.why: It is open on payment terms but blocked on list price. We currently pay late 83 % of the time and never take skonto.

trades.get: unit_price fixed at 23.13 through 2028, with no index clause
trades.why: This protects us against the investor's price review. Holding the price is not a reduction, so it fits their policy.

trades.give: Call-off flexibility: rolling forecast and agreed call-off windows
trades.get: lead_time_days cut from 28 to about 21, plus a firm 95 % OTD commitment
trades.why: It offered call-off flexibility, and its OTD of 80-88 % is below the 95 % contract target.

trades.give: volume_per_year: firm forecast of about 18,000 pcs per year
trades.why: Its ppm has improved from 400 to 271. Locking this in is cheap for it.

arguments.point: OTD has been below the 95 % contract target for four quarters (92, 80, 84, 88 %). We expect a delivery-performance commitment if price cannot move.
A skonto or payment-term structure is not a price reduction, so it stays within the head-office directive and the 2 % authority of the sales side.
Our spend is steady at about 423-434k EUR per year. We offer continuity and a longer contract in return for price stability during the ownership change.

Our should-cost estimate suggests the price is only about 2.9 % above its cost without margin. Use this softly as a reason to hold the price, not to cut it, because the estimate's confidence is only 5 %.

avoid: Demanding a list-price cut: it is frozen by head office and will just escalate or stall
Threatening to resource: there are no other sources and we are only 1.2 % of its turnover
Asking for moves above 2 % at short notice: the pricing committee meets only every two weeks
Raising payment terms without first fixing our own late payments (83 % late)
tone: Businesslike and structured. Frame offers as terms packages its contact can approve within policy, and acknowledge the ownership change.
red_flags: The new financial investor plans to review prices and terms with all customers. Expect pressure toward increases or tighter terms.

Deadline: price-change notice and contract termination both require 90 days before 2026-12-31, i.e. about 2026-10-02. Confirm that no increase notice has been received and secure the 23.13 hold in writing.
Single source (100 % quota, no other sources) for an A-class part. Supply risk if relations sour.
Delivery reliability is below target (OTD 80-88 % against 95 %).
Our payment behaviour is poor (83 % late), which weakens our position on terms.

evidence.claim: Acquired by a financial investor that plans to review prices and terms with all customers
Head office froze price reductions until Dec 2027; it is open on payment terms and call-off flexibility
Price changes above 2 % need pricing-committee approval (meets every two weeks)
Single source for part:350050 at 23.13, valid since 2026-01-01
History shows it settles far below its ask (last round asked 4.9 %, settled 3.1 %)
Contract ends 2026-12-31, auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice; price changes need 90 days' notice
OTD below the 95 % target; ppm improved from 400 to 271; EUR 150 chargeback per complaint
Financially stable: credit index unchanged at 176 and equity ratio 43.5 %, so it is not cash-short

indicators.credit_index: 176 (12 months ago 176; higher is worse, >300 weak)
